newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Treasury challenges Ruch court ruling.
newsitem.headline: Polish Treasury challenges Ruch court ruling.

text.p: Poland's Treasury Ministry said on Friday it will appeal against a Warsaw court ruling that no shares of the Ruch SA newsstand chain can be sold until a legal case involving France's Hachette has been conclusively settled.
"Of course we are appealing against this decision and we will submit a protest, that is our legal right," ministry spokesman Zbigniew Ostrowski told Reuters.
Poland is privatising Ruch, its biggest press distribution network, and the ministry in December signed a letter of intent with a consortium including Polish publishers and Hachette.
But in March the ministry annulled the earlier tender, and again invited talks on purchasing shares in Ruch, which has a 65 percent share of press distribution in Poland.

The ministry said it had put aside the deal with Hachette -- which offered to pay $83 million for the Ruch stake, increase its capital by $45 million and then invest another $155 million -- because a more attractive offer had emerged.

This month the French-Polish consortium asked the Warsaw provincial court to rule whether the letter of intent was still legally-binding and to force the ministry to honour its commitments. On Wednesday the court decided to freeze sales of Ruch shares.
Ostrowski said that regardless of the court's decision privatisation procedures could continue and the ministry was holding talks on the sale of up to 75 percent of Ruch, planned for late June.

"We can make use of the legal procedure of submitting a protest and we will do so. It is hard to say what the court's next decision will be...but we have planned to complete this (Ruch sale) at the end of June," he added.

The ministry previously said that two consortia were now shortlisted for Ruch, one of which included trading company Universal SA, the private Polsat SA television station and soft-drinks producer Multico SA.
Hachette refused to bid in the new tender saying the ministry had treated it unfairly because it invited new bids for Ruch after the French-led group had unveiled its terms.
Hachette plans to create its own distribution network in Poland if the government fails to sell it Ruch.
